scenes.title: Data Lineage & Root-Cause Analysis
scenes.subtitle: Tracing data from source to symptom
scenes.narration: Data lineage maps how data flows and transforms across systems, which makes root-cause analysis of incidents fast and reliable.

scenes.heading: Why lineage matters
bullets: Impact analysis: who is affected downstream
Root-cause analysis: where a problem originated
Change management: what breaks if we alter a table
Trust and compliance: provenance of every field
scenes.narration: Lineage enables impact analysis by revealing every downstream asset a broken table feeds. It powers root-cause analysis by letting you trace a symptom back to its origin upstream. It supports safe change management by showing what a schema edit would break, and it provides the provenance regulators and stakeholders demand.

scenes.heading: Root-cause analysis with lineage
steps: An alert fires on a downstream dashboard
Find the first asset that violates its checks
Fix the source and confirm downstream recovery
scenes.narration: Analysis starts when an alert fires on a visible downstream asset like a dashboard metric. Instead of guessing, you walk the lineage graph upstream node by node. You stop at the first asset whose own checks are failing, which is the true origin, then fix it and verify that the downstream assets recover.

scenes.heading: Table-level vs column-level lineage
scenes.narration: Table-level lineage records which tables feed which, which is inexpensive but only gives a coarse view of impact. Column-level lineage traces individual fields through transformations, enabling precise analysis of exactly which columns a change affects. The finer granularity costs more to capture but pays off during complex root-cause investigations.

scenes.text: Lineage turns root-cause analysis from guesswork into a directed walk from symptom back to source.
scenes.narration: Without lineage, diagnosing a data incident is slow and error-prone. With it, you can confidently trace both blast radius downstream and the true origin upstream.
